requirements.quote:
STREAM frames implicitly create a stream and carry stream data.  The
   Type field in the STREAM frame takes the form 0b00001XXX (or the set
   of values from 0x08 to 0x0f).  The three low-order bits of the frame
   type determine the fields that are present in the frame:
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The frame Type field is 0b00001XXX, equivalently a value from 0x08 through 0x0f inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A STREAM frame must not use a Type value outside 0x08 through 0x0f.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame type can be inspected and checked against the fixed bit pattern and numeric range.

requirements.quote:
STREAM frames implicitly create a stream and carry stream data.  The
   Type field in the STREAM frame takes the form 0b00001XXX (or the set
   of values from 0x08 to 0x0f).  The three low-order bits of the frame
   type determine the fields that are present in the frame:
requirements.condition: When interpreting a STREAM frame Type field.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the three low-order bits of the frame type to determine which conditional fields are present.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser's field-presence decisions can be compared with the three low-order type bits.

requirements.quote:
*  The OFF bit (0x04) in the frame type is set to indicate that there
      is an Offset field present.  When set to 1, the Offset field is
      present.  When set to 0, the Offset field is absent and the Stream
      Data starts at an offset of 0 (that is, the frame contains the
      first bytes of the stream, or the end of a stream that includes no
      data).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Offset field must not be omitted.
requirements.why_checkable: The OFF bit and presence of an encoded Offset field are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
*  The OFF bit (0x04) in the frame type is set to indicate that there
      is an Offset field present.  When set to 1, the Offset field is
      present.  When set to 0, the Offset field is absent and the Stream
      Data starts at an offset of 0 (that is, the frame contains the
      first bytes of the stream, or the end of a stream that includes no
      data).
requirements.required_behavior: The Offset field is absent and Stream Data starts at stream offset 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: An Offset field must not be present or a nonzero starting offset inferred.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect field absence and verify the parser assigns offset 0.

requirements.quote:
*  The LEN bit (0x02) in the frame type is set to indicate that there
      is a Length field present.  If this bit is set to 0, the Length
      field is absent and the Stream Data field extends to the end of
      the packet.  If this bit is set to 1, the Length field is present.
requirements.required_behavior: The Length field is absent and Stream Data extends through all remaining bytes of the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A Length field must not be parsed or encoded.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type, field absence, and amount of packet data consumed can be checked directly.

requirements.quote:
*  The LEN bit (0x02) in the frame type is set to indicate that there
      is a Length field present.  If this bit is set to 0, the Length
      field is absent and the Stream Data field extends to the end of
      the packet.  If this bit is set to 1, the Length field is present.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Length field must not be omitted.
requirements.why_checkable: The LEN bit and presence of the encoded Length field are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
*  The FIN bit (0x01) indicates that the frame marks the end of the
      stream.  The final size of the stream is the sum of the offset and
      the length of this frame.
requirements.condition: When the FIN bit is set in a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame as marking the end of the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream state after processing a FIN-bearing frame can be tested.

requirements.quote:
*  The FIN bit (0x01) indicates that the frame marks the end of the
      stream.  The final size of the stream is the sum of the offset and
      the length of this frame.
requirements.condition: When determining final stream size from a STREAM frame that marks the end of the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the final size to the frame offset plus the frame length.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's recorded final size can be compared with the arithmetic sum of offset and length.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST terminate the connection with error
   STREAM_STATE_ERROR if it receives a STREAM frame for a locally
   initiated stream that has not yet been created, or for a send-only
   stream.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a STREAM frame for a locally initiated stream that has not yet been created.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not accept or continue the connection after the invalid frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted frame and connection-state observation can verify both termination and the reported error code.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST terminate the connection with error
   STREAM_STATE_ERROR if it receives a STREAM frame for a locally
   initiated stream that has not yet been created, or for a send-only
   stream.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a STREAM frame for a send-only stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not accept stream data or continue the connection after the invalid frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A STREAM frame on a send-only stream can be injected and the resulting connection close and error code observed.

requirements.quote:
STREAM Frame {
     Type (i) = 0x08..0x0f,
     Stream ID (i),
     [Offset (i)],
     [Length (i)],
     Stream Data (..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or parse fields in this order: Type, Stream ID, optional Offset, optional Length, then Stream Data.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized field sequence can be inspected against the specified frame layout.

requirements.quote:
Stream ID:  A variable-length integer indicating the stream ID of the
      stream; see Section 2.1.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Stream ID field of a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the stream ID as a variable-length integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's wire encoding can be checked as a variable-length integer.

requirements.quote:
Offset:  A variable-length integer specifying the byte offset in the
      stream for the data in this STREAM frame.  This field is present
      when the OFF bit is set to 1.  When the Offset field is absent,
      the offset is 0.
requirements.condition: When an Offset field is present in a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and interpret it as a variable-length integer specifying the byte offset of the frame's data in the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The Offset wire representation and its interpretation can be tested with known stream positions.

requirements.quote:
Length:  A variable-length integer specifying the length of the
      Stream Data field in this STREAM frame.  This field is present
      when the LEN bit is set to 1.  When the LEN bit is set to 0, the
      Stream Data field consumes all the remaining bytes in the packet.
requirements.condition: When a Length field is present in a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and interpret it as a variable-length integer specifying the length of the Stream Data field.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded integer can be compared with the actual number of Stream Data bytes.

requirements.quote:
When a Stream Data field has a length of 0, the offset in the STREAM
   frame is the offset of the next byte that would be sent.
requirements.condition: When the Stream Data field has length 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the frame offset as the offset of the next byte that would be sent.
requirements.why_checkable: Given a known stream send position and a zero-length frame, the offset interpretation can be compared with the next-byte position.

requirements.quote:
The first byte in the stream has an offset of 0.  The largest offset
   delivered on a stream -- the sum of the offset and data length --
   cannot exceed 2^62-1, as it is not possible to provide flow control
   credit for that data.  Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit
   MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or
   FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When assigning the position of the first byte in a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign the first byte an offset of 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The first byte must not have a nonzero offset.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's byte-position mapping can be checked for a stream beginning at its first byte.

requirements.quote:
The first byte in the stream has an offset of 0.  The largest offset
   delivered on a stream -- the sum of the offset and data length --
   cannot exceed 2^62-1, as it is not possible to provide flow control
   credit for that data.  Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit
   MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or
   FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When encoding, accepting, or delivering data from a STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the frame offset plus data length does not exceed 2^62-1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode, accept, or deliver a largest stream offset greater than 2^62-1.
requirements.why_checkable: Offset and data length are numeric inputs whose sum can be checked against the fixed upper bound.

requirements.quote:
The first byte in the stream has an offset of 0.  The largest offset
   delivered on a stream -- the sum of the offset and data length --
   cannot exceed 2^62-1, as it is not possible to provide flow control
   credit for that data.  Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit
   MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or
   FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a received STREAM frame has an offset plus data length greater than 2^62-1.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat receipt of the frame as a connection error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not accept the frame as valid.
requirements.error_behavior: Use connection error type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame crossing the fixed numeric limit can be injected and the connection error type observed.
